analysis.investment_thesis: Himadri is a credible specialty chemicals franchise pivoting toward EV battery materials, but the underlying coal-tar business is inherently cyclical and capital-intensive, lacking the durable moat I require. At 35x trailing earnings for a business that earned only INR 39 Cr in FY22 and INR 555 Cr in FY25, the market is pricing in a successful EV transition that is far from certain.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 16.3% and operating income CAGR of 21.7% over nine years demonstrate compounding execution
Conservative balance sheet with Debt/Equity of 0.21, ROCE of 22%, and operating CF turning consistently positive (4/5 years)
Strategic pivot into anode materials and LFP cathodes for lithium-ion batteries addresses a large, structural growth market
key_risks: Earnings are deeply cyclical: net profit swung from INR 324 Cr (FY19) to INR 39 Cr (FY22), exposing dependence on steel/coking-coal industry cycles
Capital requirements are rising sharply — CWIP surged to INR 443 Cr in FY25 while cash fell to INR 50 Cr; returns on new capital are unproven
EV battery materials pivot is speculative and faces intense global competition from Chinese incumbents with massive scale advantages
red_flags: Coal tar pitch is a byproduct business tied to coke/steel production — no pricing power, no moat
Borrowings rose from INR 605 Cr to INR 864 Cr in FY25 while operating CF was only INR 447 Cr — growing capital intensity
35x P/E for a cyclical business; next steel downturn could collapse earnings back toward FY21-22 levels
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Himadri's financial trajectory is impressive on the surface — nine-year revenue CAGR of 16.3% and a clean balance sheet (D/E 0.21) — but the underlying economics of coal tar chemicals are commodity-like. The business has no pricing power of its own; it processes residues from the steel industry and sells into tyres, aluminium, and graphite electrodes, all of which are cyclical. The FY20-22 earnings collapse (operating income fell from INR 560 Cr to INR 156 Cr) is a textbook demonstration of this vulnerability.

The EV battery materials pivot — anode materials, LFP cathodes — is the real reason the stock trades at 35x earnings, and I understand the excitement. But I have two concerns: first, this segment is capital-hungry and unproven at scale; the CWIP jump to INR 443 Cr and cash dropping to INR 50 Cr signal heavy investment with uncertain returns. Second, Chinese anode manufacturers operate at costs Himadri cannot match. A wonderful business at a fair price is my standard — Himadri is a fair-to-good business at an optimistic price.
